newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER WINS IN MONZA AS HILL SPINS OUT.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER WINS IN MONZA AS HILL SPINS OUT.

text.p: Double world champion Michael Schumacher of Germany sent more than 150,000 fans into ecstacy at the Italian Grand Prix on Sunday when he drove to his first win for Ferrari in Italy since joining the team this season.
Schumacher's virtuoso performance overshadowed the battle for the world drivers' championship between Williams duo Briton Damon Hill and Canadian Jacques Villeneuve.
Hill, looking for the win that would virtually seal his first championship, made a brilliant start from pole postion but spun out of the race on only the sixth lap of the 53-lap contest.
Villeneuve also failed to add to his points total by struggling home seventh after making three pitstops in a disappointing race for the Williams team.

Schumacher notched his second successive victory, his third of the season and 22nd of his career, comfortably ahead of Frenchman and former Ferrari driver Jean Alesi who was driving for Schumacher's former team, Benetton.
Finland's Mika Hakinen in a McLaren was third ahead of the two Jordans driven by Briton Martin Brundle and Brazilian Rubens Barrichello. Another Brazilian, Pedro Dizin, finished sixth in a Ligier.
Schumacher's victory gave Ferrari their first cause for the mass celebrations which filled the track below the rostrum since Austrian Gerhard Berger won for the Marinello-based team in 1988.

The result left the two top postions in the drivers championship unchanged. But with only two races now remaining, Hill's lead of 13 points looks more commanding than it had before the start. Hill has 81 points, Villeneuve 68 and Schumacher 49.

Villeneuve now has a minimum target of one victory and a third place finish in the final two races in Portugal and Japan, with Hill failing to score in either, if he is to stop him taking the title away with him from Williams at the end of the season.
Hill was told by the Williams team only 10 days before Sunday's race that he was being dropped at the end of the year and replaced by Germany's Heinz-Harald Frentzen.
It had not seemed to affect his performance as he convincingly took pole position and made a ferocious start to the race by fighting off strong challenges to lead through the opening five laps.
But on lap six, Hill hit one of the temporary tyre barriers erected at the first chicane, lost control and spun out of the race.

"I did one of those things that there's no way out of and I have to admit to making a mistake. There's no-one to blame but myself. That should have been a fairly easy race victory but I threw it away," confessed Hill afterwards.
His departure left Alesi in the lead but the Frenchman was outwitted in pitstop strategy by Schumacher and Ferrari.

The German, who had announced before the race that his wife Corinna was expecting their first baby, took command from lap 31 and drove comfortably through to the chequered flag, reeling off a succession of fastest laps along the way.

Villeneuve also seemed to suffer from similar problems to Hill with barriers and kerbs at the chicanes and made three pitstops compared to Schumacher's one, including one which also covered a stop-go penalty for missing a chicane along the way.

The scenes at the end of the race were the most colourful and stirring seen at Monza for eight years and fortified the widely held view in Italy that the scarlet coloured team are on their way back, despite the retirement of Schumacher's team mate Eddie Irvine with what seemed to be engine problems.
"To win in front of those fans was wonderful. I've never seen so much emotion and so many people...I wish every one of them could have come up onto the podium to celebrate," said Schumacher.
"It is hard to believe this. It is fantastic, absolutely crazy," said Schumacher. "You have goose-bumps everywhere -- all over your body as you see (the crowd) there from on the track.
"I guessed the only opportunity I had to win was to wait until the first pit stops and then hope I would be able to do something then. At top speed I was not able to overtake (Alesi) to be honest.

"My car was not so good on the first set of tyres, but it behaved better on the second set. I really enjoyed the race, but I was not pushing too hard. I would say I was driving for most of the time at only about 90 percent."
The German said he had one "stupid moment" at a chicane, where the dangerously high and loose kerbs made of concrete were protected by piles of tyres.
"I knew I had a big advantage in terms of time and I had just been told by the pits to take it easy on the brakes. I just lost concentration slightly and hit the tyre.

"I was lucky today because without Damon going into the tyre barrier, it would have been a lot more difficult. Even so, looking at the lap times, we were competitive and I think we would have been able to fight with Williams."
Alesi said he was delighted to claim his eighth podium placing of the season and to finish second after starting sixth on the grid.
